Author: Abhinand Kumar Shavili

 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Abhinand Kumar Shavili
 And
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Pulla Karthik
 Writ Petition No.1808 Of 2023
Order:

(per AKS,J) Sri Jarpula Shanker, uncle of the detenu, Nenavath Vinod alias Charan, S/o. N.
Shanker, has filed the present Habeas Corpus petition challenging the detention order vide Proc.No.C2/7304/2022, dated 27.12.2022, passed by the respondent No.2-Collector and District Magistrate, Ranga Reddy District, whereby, the detenu was detained under Section 3(2) of the Telangana Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Bootleggers, Dacoits, Drug-Offenders, Goondas,
Immoral Traffic Offenders, Land-Grabbers, Spurious Seed Offenders, Insecticide Offenders,
Fertilizer Offenders, Food Adulteration Offenders, Fake Document offenders, Scheduled Commodities Offenders, Forest Offenders, Gaming Offenders, Sexual Offenders, Explosive Substances Offenders, Arms Offenders, Cyber Crime Offenders and White Collar or Financial Offenders Act, 1986 (for short, 'Act 1 of 1986'), and the consequential confirmation order vide G.O.Rt.No.271, General Administration (Spl. (Law & 2 AKS,J & PK,J Order)) Department, dated 17.02.2023, passed by the Secretary to Government, General Administration (Spl. (Law & Order))
Department, Government of Telangana.

sentences.text: 2. Heard Ms. R. Sowmya Reddy, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri S. Mujib Kumar, learned Special Government Pleader, representing the learned Additional Advocate General appearing for the respondents.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner had contended that the detenu was detained by the respondents under the provisions of the Act 1 of 1986, vide the impugned detention order, dated 27.12.2022, on the alleged ground that he was involved in three crimes i.e., Crime No.88 of 2022 of Prohibition and Excise Station, Shamshabad, Ranga Reddy District, registered for the offence under Section 8(c) read with 20(b)(ii)(A) of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985 (for short, 'NDPS Act') and Crime Nos.99 of 2022 and 128 of 2022 of Prohibition and Excise Station,
Shamshabad, Ranga Reddy District, registered for the offence under Section 8(c) read with 20(b)(ii)(B) of the NDPS Act.

Learned counsel further contended that the detenu was released on bail in Crime Nos.88 of 2022 and 99 of 2022 of Prohibition and Excise 3 AKS,J & PK,J Station,
Shamshabad.
Thereafter, he was again arrested in connection with Crime No.128 of 2022 and remanded to judicial custody on 08.12.2022.

In the said crime, the detenu has moved a bail Jarpula Shanker vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others on 13 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26519140/
1 application and the same was pending, as on the date of passing of the impugned detention order.

sentences.text: Thus, the detenu continues to be in judicial custody, as on the date of passing of the impugned detention order.

In spite of the same, the detaining authority has passed the impugned detention order, dated 27.12.2022, without appreciating the fact that the detenu is already in judicial custody and the question of detenu disturbing the peace and affecting the general public would not arise.
Therefore, the impugned orders are passed mechanically, without application of mind and they are liable to be set aside.

4. On the other hand, the learned Special Government Pleader appearing for the respondents had contended that the detaining authority can pass the detention order even though the detenu is in judicial custody.

The impugned detention order was passed on the apprehension that there is every likelihood of the detenu being granted bail in Crime No.128 of 2022 and that after release, he may indulge in similar offence.
Therefore, the detaining authority was 4 AKS,J & PK,J justified in passing the impugned detention order.
However, subsequently, the bail application moved by the detenu in Crime No.128 of 2022 was dismissed by the competent criminal Court.
Therefore, there are no merits in the Writ Petition and the same is liable to be dismissed.

5. This Court, having considered the rival submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties,
is of the view that, as on the date of passing of the impugned detention order, the detenu was in judicial remand and even today, he is in judicial remand.
Therefore, the detaining authority ought not to have passed the detention order against such an individual.
Hence, the impugned orders are liable to be set aside.
6. In the result, the Writ Petition is allowed.

The impugned detention order vide Proc.No.C2/7304/2022, dated 27.12.2022, passed by the respondent No.2, and the consequential confirmation order vide G.O.Rt.No.271, General Administration (Spl. (Law & Order)) Department,
dated 17.02.2023, passed by the Secretary to Government, General Administration (Spl. (Law &
Order)) Department, Government of Telangana, are hereby set aside.
5 AKS,J & PK,J
However, it is made clear that since the detenu is already in judicial custody, the question of setting him free does not arise.
There shall be no order as to costs.

Miscellaneous Petitions, if any, pending in this Writ Petition shall stand closed.
___________________________ ABHINAND KUMAR SHAVILI, J _________________ PULLA KARTHIK, J Date: 13-03-2023.
